claim: Server-side encryption in Kinesis Data Streams encrypts data with an AWS KMS key you specify before it is at rest. Data is encrypted before it is written to the stream storage layer and decrypted after it is retrieved from storage.
question: When is data encrypted and decrypted with Kinesis Data Streams server-side encryption?

values.display: encrypted before it's written to the Kinesis stream storage layer
decrypted after it’s retrieved from storage

evidence.quote: Server-side encryption is a feature in Amazon Kinesis Data Streams that automatically encrypts data before it's at rest by using an AWS KMS customer master key (CMK) you specify. Data is encrypted before it's written to the Kinesis stream storage layer, and decrypted after it’s retrieved from storage.

claim: With server-side encryption, Kinesis stream producers and consumers do not need to manage master keys or cryptographic operations, because data is encrypted automatically as it enters and leaves the service.

automatically encrypted as it enters and leaves

evidence.quote: With server-side encryption, your Kinesis stream producers and consumers don't need to manage master keys or cryptographic operations. Your data is automatically encrypted as it enters and leaves the Kinesis Data Streams service, so your data at rest is encrypted.

a master key imported into the AWS KMS service

evidence.quote: AWS KMS makes it easy to use a CMK for Kinesis that is managed by AWS, a user-specified AWS KMS CMK, or a master key imported into the AWS KMS service.

claim: You can attach a resource-based policy to a data stream to grant access to another account, IAM user or IAM role. A resource-based policy must name a principal.
question: How do you give another AWS account access to a Kinesis data stream?

values.display: Attach a resource-based policy to your data stream
must specify a principal

evidence.quote: Attach a [resource-based policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html#policies_resource-based) to your data stream to grant access to another account, IAM user, or IAM role. Resource-based policies are JSON policy documents that you attach to a resource such as a data stream.
You must specify a principal in a resource-based policy.

claim: When the principal and the data stream are in separate accounts, you must also use an identity-based policy to grant the principal access. If the resource-based policy grants access to a principal in the same account, no additional identity-based policy is required.
question: Is a resource-based policy on the stream enough for a principal in another account?

values.display: must also use an identity-based policy
no additional identity-based policy is required

qualifiers.condition: principal and resource in separate AWS accounts

evidence.quote: Adding a cross-account principal to a resource-based policy is only half of establishing the trust relationship. When the principal and the resource are in separate AWS accounts, you must also use an identity-based policy to grant the principal access to the resource. However, if a resource-based policy grants access to a principal in the same account, no additional identity-based policy is required.
